arxiv-2108-10055.title: Universal Scalar Leptoquark Action for Matching
arxiv-2108-10055.creator: Athanasios Dedes, Kostas Mantzaropoulos
arxiv-2108-10055.description: Abstract In this study we present a universal effective action for one-loop matching of all scalar leptoquarks. We use both the Universal One-Loop Effective Action (UOLEA) and covariant diagrams to evaluate the Wilson coefficients directly in the Green basis for up-to dimension-6 operators.

arxiv-2203-13137.description: Abstract We study the discrepancy between the distribution of a vector-valued functional of i.i.d. random elements and that of a Gaussian vector. Our main contribution is an explicit bound on the convex distance between the two distributions, holding in every dimension.

arxiv-2405-09790.title: Supermassive black hole formation from Affleck-Dine mechanism with suppressed clustering on large scales
arxiv-2405-09790.creator: Kentaro Kasai, Masahiro Kawasaki, Kai Murai, Shunsuke Neda
arxiv-2405-09790.description: Abstract We study a primordial black hole (PBH) formation model based on the framework of the inhomogeneous Affleck-Dine (AD) mechanism, which can explain the seeds of supermassive black holes (SMBHs). This model, however, predicts strong clustering of SMBHs that is inconsistent with the observation of angular correlation of quasars.

arxiv-2502-04320.description: Abstract Do the rich representations of multi-modal diffusion transformers (DiTs) exhibit unique properties that enhance their interpretability? We introduce ConceptAttention , a novel method that leverages the expressive power of DiT attention layers to generate high-quality saliency maps that precisely locate textual concepts within images.

arxiv-2509-21937.title: Some stability results for the fractional differential equations with two delays
arxiv-2509-21937.creator: Pragati Dutta, Sachin Bhalekar
arxiv-2509-21937.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Pragati Dutta, Sachin Bhalekar. This paper investigates the stability properties of a nonlinear fractional differential equation with two discrete delays and a delay-dependent coefficient. Such equations arise in various biological and control systems where temporal delays influence feedback mechanisms. Two cases are analyzed: one where the first delay is zero, and the second acts through an exponential coefficient, and another where the first delay is fixed. We derive delay-independent stability conditions using linearization, characteristic equations, and bifurcation theory, along with complete theoretical proofs.

arxiv-2510-08079.title: A Unified Approach to Quantum Key Leasing with a Classical Lessor
arxiv-2510-08079.creator: Fuyuki Kitagawa, Jiahui Liu, Shota Yamada, Takashi Yamakawa
arxiv-2510-08079.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Fuyuki Kitagawa, Jiahui Liu, Shota Yamada, Takashi Yamakawa. Secure key leasing allows a cryptographic key to be leased as a quantum state in such a way that the key can later be revoked in a verifiable manner. In this work, we propose a modular framework for constructing secure key leasing with a classical-lessor, where the lessor is entirely classical and, in particular, the quantum secret key can be both leased and revoked using only classical communication.

pmc-12963949.title: Phenological shifts and increases in voltinism within a moth community over a century of anthropogenic change
pmc-12963949.creator: Emma M. Foster, Jason J. Dombroskie, Christopher A. Halsch, Thomas H. Q. Powell, Eliza M. Grames
pmc-12963949.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In temperate ecosystems, warming temperatures can advance spring phenology, extend autumn phenology, disrupt dormancy regulation, result in phenological mismatch across taxa, and even lead to increases in the number of generations per year (i.e., increases in voltinism). Much of what we know about the impacts of global change on species phenology and voltinism comes from recent decades; however, anthropogenic warming began centuries ago.

pmc-13611328.creator: Hongyan Sun, Jialu Fan, Yujing Zhang, Jun Xing, Yinlian Zhang, Cunxiang Ju, Juan Liang
pmc-13611328.description: Immunodeficient and humanized mouse models have become essential tools for investigating human immunity, disease pathogenesis, and therapeutic evaluation. uslaw-usc-t49-s31503.description: United States Code, Title 49 (Transportation); Part B (Commercial); Chapter 315 (Motor Carrier Safety). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) General Authority.— The Secretary of Transportation may investigate and report on the need for regulation by the United States Government of sizes, weight, and combinations of motor vehicles and qualifications and maximum hours of service of employees of a motor carrier subject.
